name: scanruler-mcp

tools.name: scanruler_status
tools.description: Whether a ScanRuler page is connected to this agent, which version and plugins it has, whether its tab is hidden (page.hidden), and — when none is — how the user connects one. backend says whether ScanRuler runs in a tab (page) or in this server (headless). jobs lists the latest calls that change the session, newest first, each running, done or failed — a call whose answer you did not get is among them; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer.

tools.name: scanruler_open
tools.description: Open ScanRuler in the user’s default browser, paired with this server, and wait for the page to connect — for when scanruler_status says none is. The first time, the browser asks the user whether the site may reach apps on this computer; they must allow it. Returns the status, with opened: whether the browser was asked to open it. If connected is still false, tell the user what howToConnect says.

tools.name: scanruler_wait
tools.description: Wait until a ScanRuler page is connected (for: "page", the default), or until it is also done with what it is busy with and every change still running has finished (for: "idle" — then finished lists the changes done or failed since the last such answer, a failed one with its error), or until a job is done (for: "job" with job — a call started with wait: false, or one whose answer did not come; scanruler_status lists them). Returns the status, or for a job its answer: { job, tool, state, ms, result } or { …, error: { code, message } } — state running if the time ran out first. connected is false if the time ran out waiting for a page.

job.description: The job to wait for, with for: "job" — as a call with wait: false or scanruler_status gave it.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait at most, seconds — 120 by default.

tools.name: scanruler_batch
tools.description: Run several of the ScanRuler tools in one call, in order, each with its own arguments — a run of scan_nearest, element_fit or section_get calls, say. Returns results, one per call in order: { tool, ok, result } or { tool, ok: false, error: { code, message } }. The first refused stops the rest (stopped says which index) unless stopOnError is false — and then, with rollback (the default), every change the batch made before it is undone, so the batch stands or falls whole: the answer names failed: { index, tool, error } and undone (the steps taken back, newest first). Each call that changes the session is still its own undo step. timings: true gives each call its ms and the batch total_ms, and a change's build the steps it played with their ms (result.steps.played). wait: false answers at once with { queued, job }; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives the batch's answer. A tool that returns a picture gives its text here, the picture written to a file only if its call gave path. The server’s own tools (scanruler_status, _open, _wait, _batch) cannot be batched.

tool.description: A tool’s name, as listed — scan_nearest, element_fit.

arguments.description: Its arguments, as the tool takes them; {} for none.

stopOnError.description: Stop at the first refused call (the default), or run every call and report each.

rollback.description: When the batch stops at a refused call, undo what it changed before it (the default) — or leave those changes standing (false).

timings.description: Each call’s ms, the batch’s total_ms, and the steps a change’s build played with their ms.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

tools.name: align_auto
tools.description: Read a coordinate system off the scan and apply it, as Auto-align then Confirm alignment do: the directions most faces are square to and the axis round walls run along, the part standing on its base, its long side along X. Returns what the pose was read from, the transform and how many elements moved with it. One undo step.

detail.description: brief (the default): the transform and how many elements moved with the part. full: every element where it now is, as the list gives it.

tools.name: align_datum
tools.description: A 3-2-1 alignment, as the panel’s alignment box sets it up: primary levels the part — a plane (or 3 points on a face) whose outward normal becomes primaryAxis (default z-, the face the part stands on facing down); secondary turns it — a line, axis or plane (or 2 points along an edge) laid along secondaryAxis (default x+); origin is the zero point — a point, sphere or circle (or 1 point). Each is an element by id or name, or points on the scan in mm. An origin alone moves the part without turning it. Everything measured moves with the part. Returns the transform applied — the whole alignment the part carries, when it was aligned before — and how many elements moved with it. One undo step.

Refuses when the scan has no symmetry plane. Returns the note on what it settled on, the transform and how many elements moved with it. One undo step.

tools.name: deviation_align
tools.description: Rigid best fit (no scale) of the scan onto the reference part, then the deviation map under it. mode auto (the default) finds the pose on its own; points starts from three or more pairs of corresponding points — a point on the scan and the same point on the reference, mm — then refines; local refines the fit in hand on a marked surface only (vertices, scan vertex numbers), within searchDistance mm. Returns the alignment (RMS, points matched, transform) and the map’s statistics. One undo step.

reference.description: The same point on the reference, mm.

vertices.description: local: the marked surface, scan vertex numbers.

searchDistance.description: local: how far a point may be from the reference to count, mm.

tools.name: deviation_hotspots
tools.description: The deviation map read as patches: the scan vertices whose deviation lies past the tolerance (the map’s own, under deviation.settings, unless tolerance says otherwise) gathered into connected regions, the largest and farthest first — where the part is off, how large each place is and by how much, instead of one number over the whole part. Each patch: its centre and box in mm (in the frame the scan is measured in — what scan.query { box } and element.fit take), its area, how many vertices, the mean and the extreme deviation and which side (outside the reference or inside), the point of the extreme and the scan vertex there, and a few of its vertices (what element.fit_marked takes). With a map against the reference part the patch’s centre and extreme are given on the reference too (onReference — what the Deviation workspace shows and view.render { frame } takes there). grain is how close two vertices over tolerance have to be to be one patch, three point spacings by default. found and over say how many patches and vertices over tolerance there were in all — within the search distance, the vertices the map draws as a measurement. Then far, the vertices past the search distance, which the map draws bare: read it every time — far.inside is the scan deeper inside the reference than the search distance, where the reference has material the part has not (a hole, a pocket or a slot the model lacks), far.outside the scan further off it, where the part has what the model has not, or scan spray; each with its count and its patches, the largest first, and far.count both together; unmeasured says how many vertices the facing limit left without a reading. Needs a deviation map (deviation.align, or deviation.set_target). Changes nothing.

tolerance.description: ± mm; the map’s tolerance by default.

patches.description: How many patches to name; 8 by default, 50 at most.

grain.description: mm — how close two vertices over tolerance have to be to be one patch; three point spacings by default.

annotations.title: Where the deviation lies over tolerance

The elements measured on the scan stay. Returns the deviation state. Not undoable: a new reference starts a new history. The file is read from `path` on this computer and streamed to the page.

tools.name: deviation_set_target

Needs the viewport. Returns the map’s statistics. One undo step.

tools.name: deviation_settings

Returns the deviation state. One undo step.

tools.name: dimension_add
tools.description: Measure between elements, or a size or tolerance of one, as the panel’s dimension box does. refs are the elements by id or name. Without type, the type follows the elements as clicking them in the viewport does — two spheres or points give their centre distance, two planes their distance, a plane and an axis their distance, and so on. With type, it is one of: dist-point-point (From, To); dist-point-axis (Point, Axis); dist-point-plane (Point, Plane); dist-axis-axis (Axis A, Axis B); dist-axis-plane (Axis, Plane); dist-plane-plane (From, To); angle-axis-axis (Axis A, Axis B); angle-axis-plane (Axis, Plane); angle-plane-plane (Plane A, Plane B); size-diameter (Feature); form-flatness (Plane); form-cylindricity (Cylinder); form-circularity (Circle); form-sphericity (Sphere); orient-parallelism (Feature, Datum); orient-perpendicularity (Feature, Datum); orient-angularity (Feature, Datum); loc-coaxiality (Feature, Datum axis). anchor, for two spheres: center (default), gap or span. limit holds the value to a ceiling or a nominal ± band. Returns the dimension with its value (mm or degrees, finer than the panel shows it), the formatted value the panel shows, and the verdict. One undo step.

tools.name: element_construct
tools.description: Construct an element from others and typed-in numbers, as the panel’s creation methods do — by kind: point (point-coords, point-centroid, point-midpoint, point-line-plane), line (line-two-points, line-axis, line-plane-plane), plane (plane-three-points, plane-offset, plane-midplane, plane-coords, plane-symmetry), circle (circle-plane-cylinder, circle-plane-sphere, circle-coords). refs fill the method’s slots in order, by element id or name; params are its numbers in order (or by key: x, y, z; offset; nx, ny, nz, px, py, pz; d, cx, cy, cz). point-centroid and plane-symmetry measure the scan themselves: vertices confines them to a marked surface, seed starts the symmetry search from a plane. plane-symmetry finds the scan’s own mirror plane as an element, the alignment left as it is (align.symmetry re-poses the part on it instead), and answers with the search’s residual: symmetry { rms, matched, sampled } and a note. Returns the element. One undo step.

tools.name: element_fit
tools.description: Fit an element on the scan where the panel would take a click: a plane, sphere, cylinder, cone or torus grows its surface from the place given and is best-fitted to it; a point is the place itself; a circle goes through three or more places. `at` is one place, or a list — a feature seen in patches can be seeded on each. A place is { vertex } (a scan vertex), { point: [x, y, z] } (the nearest scan vertex to a point, mm, in the current frame), or { screen } / { candidate } (not available yet). Returns the element with its fit and the seed actually used (vertex and point), so a recipe can be replayed on another scan. One undo step.

Points, circles and arcs count as their point (centre), lines as lines. Without type, the first that takes the two elements in the order given. Returns the dimensions on the sheet. One undo step.

tools.name: flat_edges
tools.description: The edge chains detected on the sheet, by number — what flat.fit takes as chains and flat.render writes beside each. Each with its length, whether it closes on itself, how many points and the box round it, in the sheet’s units; the longest first, or with near the nearest first, each with its point nearest that place and how far (within reach only, when given). box keeps the chains that enter it, minLength the long ones. tolerance adds each chain’s polyline, thinned to stray no further than that (5000 points at most over all). limit chains at most, 50 by default. The numbers hold until the edges are found again. Changes nothing.

box.description: Only chains with a point in this box.

reach.description: With near: only chains this close.

minLength.description: Only chains at least this long.

tolerance.description: Add each chain’s polyline, thinned to this.

tools.name: flat_edit
tools.description: Change one thing on the 2D sheet, named by its id (or name): an element, a dimension or a count takes a new name; a note new text or a new place (at, its lower-left corner); any of them visible: false to leave it out of the stage, the picture and the exports, true to bring it back. Returns the 2D state. One undo step.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

tools.name: flat_fit
tools.description: Make a 2D element on the sheet as its tool does — kind point, line, circle, arc or spline, by a method of that kind: point: flat-point-pick (pick), flat-point-midpoint (construct), flat-point-intersect (construct), flat-point-center (construct); line: flat-line-pick (pick), flat-line-seed (seed), flat-line-edge (edge); circle: flat-circle-pick (pick), flat-circle-seed (seed), flat-circle-edge (edge); arc: flat-arc-pick (pick), flat-arc-edge (edge); spline: flat-spline-pick (pick). A pick method takes points, the places clicked — each snapped to the nearest detected edge within reach unless snap: false, and the answer’s picks say where each landed and on which chain. A seed method takes one place on a detected edge and grows along it; an edge method a place on an edge, taken whole. The edge methods also take chains — whole edge chains by number (flat.edges, flat.render) — and box, every edge point inside it (of those chains only, with both); the kind’s edge method is the default then. A construct method takes refs, other 2D elements by id or name. Returns the element with its fit. One undo step.

method.description: The method — see the description; the kind’s first pick method by default.

items.description: A place on the sheet, [x, y] in the sheet’s units.

points.description: The places, in the sheet’s units.

chains.description: Edge chains by number, taken whole — for an edge or seed method.

box.description: Edge points inside this box, in the sheet’s units — for an edge or seed method.

snap.description: Picks snap to the nearest edge within reach — true by default, as the panel’s Snap box is.

reach.description: How far a place reaches for an edge, in the sheet’s units — ten image pixels by default.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms (the call, start to answer) and, where the change built, steps.played — each step the build played with its ms (steps.restored counts those taken up from a kept state, not played).

tools.name: flat_note_add

One line, as the tool writes it: a line break is written as " / ". at is its lower-left corner, in the sheet’s units. It is drawn on the stage and in flat.render, written into the SVG and DXF exports and listed in the report. Returns the note with its id. One undo step.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

tools.name: flat_objects
tools.description: The separate parts lying on the flatbed image, parted from the background by a grey level (Otsu’s, unless threshold is given; dark says the parts are darker than the background, read off the image’s border by default) and numbered in reading order — rows from the top, left to right. Each with its area (holes left out) and holes, box, centroid, equivalentDiameter (of a circle of its area), feret — the largest and smallest caliper widths and the directions they are measured along, degrees from +X — axisAngle (its long axis, degrees), and chains, the edge chains along its outline, longest first. minArea drops smaller ones: 1 mm² by default, or its pixels at 600 dpi on an image with no scale. outline adds each outline as a polygon thinned to that tolerance. flat.profile takes an object by its number. limit, 100 by default. Changes nothing.

dark.description: The parts are darker than the background.

minArea.description: The smallest part, in the sheet’s units squared.

outline.description: Add each outline, thinned to this, in the sheet’s units.

tools.name: flat_open_image
tools.description: Open a flatbed scan of a part — PNG or JPEG, at the highest optical resolution — on the 2D sheet, in place of the image there was. The scale it declares about itself is taken until it is calibrated. Needs the browser. Returns the 2D state. Not undoable: a new image starts a new history. The file is read from `path` on this computer and streamed to the page.

name.description: The file's name with its extension — "part.png". It is what the session calls the model. Defaults to the file's own name.

path.description: The file to read, on this computer: an absolute path, or one relative to the folder the agent works in.

tools.name: flat_profile
tools.description: An outline read against a centre or along an axis, and its peaks counted — the teeth of a knurl or a gear. The outline: an object of the last flat.objects by number, or edge chains by number (several make one). radial (the default): its radius against the angle about about — a circle, arc or point — or about the outline’s own centre: a part standing upright, seen from above. axial: its distance from about — a line — or from the outline’s own long axis, against the position along it, each side apart (left and right of the axis’ direction): a part lying on its side. A peak counts when it stands prominence above the higher of the valleys either side — by default 0.3 of the profile’s spread, never under the outline’s noise. Returns per side the count, the pitch (degrees round, or along the axis), the envelope (largest, smallest, mean peak, mean valley; radial also as diameters) and every peak’s angle or position and place; points adds the sampled profile. mark: true puts a count on the sheet with a numbered pick on every peak, to check by eye — one undo step; otherwise nothing changes.

object.description: An object of the last flat.objects, by number.

chains.description: Edge chains by number, as one outline.

about.description: A circle, arc or point to read the radius about, or a line to read the distance from.

axis.description: Without about: radial about the outline’s centre (the default), or axial along its long axis.

samples.description: Bins round the turn, or along the axis — from the point count by default.

prominence.description: How far a peak must stand out, in the sheet’s units.

mark.description: Put a count on every peak.

tools.description: Remove elements, dimensions, notes and counts from the 2D sheet, each by id or name (a note by id) — all of them or none. An element built on a removed one stays and says it has lost its source, and a dimension on one turns invalid, as in the panel; the answer names them. Returns what is left. One undo step.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

tools.description: A picture of the 2D sheet as a PNG, drawn as the sheet lies in the sheet’s own units — +X right, +Y up, whatever the stage’s alignment or turns — with a grid ruled in those units and its values written along the top and left edges. map says where it lies: picture pixel (column c, row r from the top) is the sheet place [left + c·unitsPerPx, top − r·unitsPerPx], to hand straight back as a place. frame zooms in on a box. show puts layers in or out: image, edges (the detected chains — as the panel shows them by default), chains (their numbers, as flat.fit and flat.edges name them), elements (with counts and the alignment), dimensions, notes, labels (names and readings), grid. width and height in pixels: the frame’s shape at most 800 on its long side by default, up to 2048. Needs the browser. The picture comes back as an image; with `path` it is written to a file too.

tools.name: flat_set_alignment

tools.name: history_redo

tools.description: Undo every step made since history.checkpoint gave this checkpoint, newest first, as the undo key would one by one — so a run of changes that went wrong in the middle is taken back whole. Refused, undoing nothing, when the mark is no longer under the steps on top — undone past it, or the history started afresh (a scan or a project opened). Returns the steps undone, newest first, and the session afterwards.

The file is read from `path` on this computer and streamed to the page.

tools.name: project_rename
tools.description: Give the project a name — what Save Project saves it under, the stem of every export and the browser tab’s title, kept in the project file. An empty name takes it off, and the scan’s or the image’s name stands in again. session.state reads it as project.name.

name.description: The name; empty takes it off.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms (the call, start to answer) and, where the change built, steps.played — each step the build played with its ms (steps.restored counts those taken up from a kept state, not played).

tools.name: project_save
tools.description: The session as a .scanruler project file, as Save Project downloads it: the scan, the reference, the image and every measurement, each rebuilt when it is opened. Needs the browser. Returns the file’s bytes and its name. The file is written to `path`; the result says where and how large it is, not its bytes.

path.description: Where to write the file: a file path, or a folder to write it into under the name ScanRuler gives it. Without it, it goes into /pkg.

tools.name: report_get
tools.description: The measurement report. format "text" is word for word what the workspace’s Copy report button puts on the clipboard — measure (elements and dimensions with verdicts), deviation, thickness or flat (2D). format "json" (the default) is the whole session’s report structured: what the numbers rest on (units, scale, frame, applied alignment, fit method and each element’s outlier cut-off), every element with its fit, every dimension with value, unit, limit and pass/fail verdict, the tally of checks, the sections, and the deviation, thickness and 2D results with their settings.

workspace.description: For text: whose report — measure (the default), deviation, thickness or flat.

tools.name: scan_fit_surface
tools.description: A patch of the scan measured as a surface — a sloped side, a twisted ruled face, a dome, a saddle, a fairing — the points given as vertices (from scan.query or a patch) or as a box (normal keeps those facing a way, within withinDeg, 30 by default). The best plane through them sets the patch’s own frame: origin at their centroid, normal (w) out of it, basisU and basisV in it, all in the frame the part is measured in now. Each model is a height over (u, v) along the normal: plane h = a + b·u + c·v; bilinear + d·u·v (a hyperbolic paraboloid: a straight-lined twisted face); quadric + d·u² + e·u·v + f·v² (a dome, bowl, saddle or a cylinder’s strip). Each answers its coefficients, rms and worst (mm off along the normal); the quadric also curvature: k1 and k2 (1/mm, the larger first), r1 and r2 (their radii, null where flat), axis1 and axis2 (their directions in the world) and shape (flat, cylinder, dome or saddle) at the patch’s middle. model: one of them, or best (the default) — every one, and best names the simplest whose rms is within a tenth of the lowest: the model that holds, plain. At most limit points are fitted (20000), spread evenly. Changes nothing.

vertices.description: The scan vertices of the patch.

box.description: The patch as the scan inside a box, in place of vertices.

normal.description: With box: only the vertices facing this way.

model.description: Which surface; best (the default) fits each and names the simplest that holds.

limit.description: How many points at most; 20000 by default.

annotations.title: Fit a sloped or curved patch

tools.name: scan_nearest
tools.description: Where a location lands on the scan: the vertex (a point snaps to the nearest one), its coordinates and outward normal, a triangle it is a corner of, and how far it is from the point asked about. Use it to check a point lies on the surface before fitting there.

vertex.description: A scan vertex, as a project file and session.state name it.

point.description: A point in millimetres, in the frame the part is measured in now; the scan vertex nearest it is taken.

screen.description: A pixel of the viewport, x right and y down from its top left, as on a view.render picture.

annotations.title: Find a place on the scan

tools.name: scan_open
tools.description: Open a mesh as the scan to measure — STL, PLY or OBJ — in place of the one there is; everything measured on the old one goes with it, so it refuses while the session holds measurements unless discard is true. Returns the scan: name, units, vertex and triangle counts, its bounding box (min and max corners), the box’s centre and its diagonal (size), in millimetres. Not undoable: a new scan starts a new history. The file is read from `path` on this computer and streamed to the page.

name.description: The file's name with its extension — "ballbar.stl". It is what the session calls the model. Defaults to the file's own name.

units.description: What the file’s coordinates are in: mm (the default), cm, m or in. An STL carries no units of its own; PLY and OBJ are taken in millimetres unless told otherwise. Everything is measured in millimetres once read.

discard.description: Replace the session even though it holds measurements — they are lost (a project file saved before keeps them). Without it the command refuses when there is work to lose.

path.description: The file to read, on this computer: an absolute path, or one relative to the folder the agent works in.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms (the call, start to answer) and, where the change built, steps.played — each step the build played with its ms (steps.restored counts those taken up from a kept state, not played).

tools.name: scan_query
tools.description: The scan’s vertices inside a box, or within a radius of a point, with their outward normals — the points on a face, to measure a dimension or a draft angle off, or to see what the scan has where a model is being built. normal keeps only the vertices facing a direction (within withinDeg, 30 by default): the top face alone, say. At most limit come back (1000 by default, 20000 at most): past it every k-th matching vertex is kept, spread evenly, and step says which k. Returns how many matched, the vertices kept (their numbers, as scan.nearest and element.fit_marked name them), their points and normals in millimetres, in the frame the part is measured in now, the box round the points kept, their centroid and mean normal. Changes nothing.

box.description: A box in the frame the part is measured in now.

near.description: A ball about a point — in place of box.

withinDeg.description: How far from it a normal may lean, degrees; 30 by default.

normal.description: Keep only the vertices whose outward normal faces this way.

limit.description: How many vertices at most; 1000 by default, 20000 at most.

tools.name: section_cut
tools.description: Cut the scan with a plane and keep the cut as a section, measured in the 2D workspace (flat) — where it is put on the sheet. across is what the plane is taken across: an element with a direction (a plane, cylinder, cone, line or circle) by id or name, or a coordinate plane "XY", "YZ" or "ZX", which is laid through the part’s centre. offset slides the plane along its normal, mm — from the element, or for a coordinate plane the coordinate itself. Returns the section: its plane and how many chains the cut has. One undo step.

oneOf.description: The element’s name, as the list shows it — "Sphere 1".

across.description: An element with a direction, or a coordinate plane "XY", "YZ", "ZX".

offset.description: Where along the normal the plane lies, mm.

name.description: A name for it; otherwise it is numbered — "Section 2".

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms (the call, start to answer) and, where the change built, steps.played — each step the build played with its ms (steps.restored counts those taken up from a kept state, not played).

tools.name: section_get
tools.description: A section’s cut as the polylines it is: each chain’s points in order, as the 2D sheet lays them flat — [u, v] millimetres in the section’s plane, what flat.fit and a sketch on the section take — and, with space "world" or "both", as [x, y, z] in the frame the part is measured in now. With them the plane (origin, normal, basisU, basisV: a sheet point is origin + u·basisU + v·basisV), and for each chain whether it is closed (a loop; its first point is repeated at the end), its length along the path, how many points it has and the box round it on the sheet. At most limit points come back over all the chains (4000 by default, 50000 at most): past it every k-th point of a chain is kept, its ends always, and step says which k. chains picks chains by their index. Changes nothing.

oneOf.description: The section’s name, as the list shows it — "Section 1".

section.description: The section, by id or name.

chains.description: Which chains; every one when left out.

space.description: sheet (the default): [u, v] on the section’s plane; world: [x, y, z]; both.

limit.description: How many points at most, over every chain asked for; 4000 by default, 50000 at most.

tools.name: section_render
tools.description: A picture of a section as a PNG, for checking a slice against what was built on it: the scan’s cut as points on the section’s sheet ([u, v] mm as section.get gives them, +u right, +v up), a grid ruled in millimetres with its values at the top and left margins, a scale bar, and over it what the workspaces’ layers draw — a model’s cut by the section’s plane as outlines, a sketch’s pieces on the section with their ids. Every scan point within ten tolerances of an outline is read against it: on it within ± tolerance (grey), or off it (red), outside the outline or inside it; points with no outline near are pale. The answer gives gap: points (the cut’s), read, over (red), outside and inside (of a closed outline — inside is scan within the model’s material, so the model stands proud there; outside, the model is short), max and rms (mm) and overBox (the sheet box round the red, to frame the next look); layers: each layer drawn by key, its outlines and pieces counted; map: picture pixel (column c, row r from the top) is the sheet place [left + c·unitsPerPx, top − r·unitsPerPx]. section names a section; or plane { origin, normal } cuts the scan there for the picture alone — no section is made, the sheet’s u and v any pair square to the normal (the answer’s sheet gives them). frame { at: [u, v], size } looks at a square of the sheet; everything by default. tolerance: the Deviation workspace’s by default. layers: the keys to draw; every one by default, [] for the scan alone. 800 px on the long side by default, up to 2048. Needs the browser. Changes nothing. The picture comes back as an image; with `path` it is written to a file too.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

plane.description: A plane to cut the scan by for the picture alone, in place of a section.

at.description: The sheet place in the middle, [u, v] mm.

size.description: The side of the square looked at, mm.

frame.description: Look at a square of the sheet.

tolerance.description: ± mm a scan point may lie off the outlines and still be on them.

layers.description: The layers to draw, by key; every one by default.

path.description: Also write the picture to a file: a file path, or a folder to write it into under the name ScanRuler gives it. Without it, it is only shown.

tools.name: session_reset
tools.description: Close the scan, the reference part and the 2D image, and with them every measurement and the project’s name, as opening an empty project does. Refuses while the session holds measurements unless discard is true. Not undoable: the history starts over too.

discard.description: Replace the session even though it holds measurements — they are lost (a project file saved before keeps them). Without it the command refuses when there is work to lose.

wait.description: false: answer at once with { queued: true, job } while the change runs on; scanruler_wait { for: "job", job } gives its answer. true (the default): answer once it is done.

timings.description: true: the answer adds ms (the call, start to answer) and, where the change built, steps.played — each step the build played with its ms (steps.restored counts those taken up from a kept state, not played).

tools.name: session_state
tools.description: The whole session as JSON: the app and its plugins, the workspace on screen, whether it is busy, the scan (file, units, vertex and triangle counts, bounding box, centre, size, applied alignment), every element with its fit, every dimension with its value, limit and verdict, the sections, what is open in the panels, the deviation, wall thickness and 2D Measure state with their statistics, the guided hint for the next step, and the undo history. Lengths in millimetres, angles in degrees. Read it before acting and after.

tools.name: thickness_measure
tools.description: Measure the wall thickness at every point of the scan, as the Wall Thickness workspace’s Measure button does, with the search settings given or those in hand. Returns the statistics (min, max, mean, sigma, share under the thin-wall limit, points measured) and the settings. One undo step.

maxThickness.description: The thickest wall searched for, mm.

normalDeviationDeg.description: How far the far wall may turn from facing back, degrees, or null to accept whatever is hit.

tools.name: view_render
tools.description: A picture of the 3D view as a PNG — what the person sees in the viewport, without the HTML labels over it (dimension values, names). Give view and/or fit to turn the view first, as view.set does, or frame to frame a box or a place. show puts the scan, the reference, the sections, the elements or the labels on screen or away for the picture alone, by key — { scan: false } pictures what was built on the scan on its own; view.set lists the keys. section cuts everything open for the picture alone, as view.set does. width and height in pixels: the viewport’s own shape at most 800 pixels on its long side by default, enough to check a step by — ask for more (up to 2048) for a picture to keep; one of them alone keeps the viewport’s shape. Waits for the session to settle first. Needs the viewport. The picture comes back as an image; with `path` it is written to a file too.

tools.name: workspace_set
tools.description: Put a workspace on screen: measure (fitting elements and dimensions), deviation (scan against a reference part or an element), thickness (wall thickness), flat (2D measuring of an image or a section), or a plugin’s by its id — session.state lists them under app.plugins. Commands put their own workspace on screen; this is for showing the person something.

instructions: These tools drive ScanRuler, a measuring app for 3D scans, in the browser tab the user has open: the user watches every step in the viewport and can undo it there. Start with scanruler_status. If no ScanRuler page is connected, call scanruler_open: it opens ScanRuler in the user’s browser, paired with this server, and waits for it. If that leaves it unconnected, tell the user what howToConnect says, then call scanruler_wait. Read session_state before acting and after: the scan’s bounding box says where the part lies, the elements and dimensions what is measured. Lengths are millimetres, angles degrees; answers give numbers to six significant digits. A place on the scan is { point: [x, y, z] } (the nearest scan vertex is taken) or { vertex: n }. To fit a feature, aim at its middle, not at an edge. Every tool that changes the session is one step of the undo history; history_undo takes the last back. report_get gives the report as JSON (format "json") or as the text the panel copies (format "text"). view_render shows you the 3D view as a picture; view_set turns it to a standard view or fits it. scanruler_batch runs several tools in one call, in order — many scan_nearest or element_fit calls, say — and stops at the first that is refused unless told to go on.
